card.band: 8h. The opcode core is simple; flag-dependent consensus and policy rules, taproot and error-code fidelity are the long tail. Scores climb steadily by flag and script type. A weaker model stalls on segwit and taproot.
card.cheat: Hidden vectors are random scripts and flag combinations, so the public JSON cannot be memorised. No bitcoin library is in the image and there is no network.
card.grading: The repo's script_tests, tx_valid/tx_invalid and sighash vectors (several thousand), plus hidden vectors generated by the real C++ interpreter over random scripts and flag combinations. The result is accepted or rejected, with the error code compared.
card.reference: Port of the upstream C++ interpreter (about 2.5k lines of Rust). The reference passes every vector.
card.task: /app ships the data-driven test vectors for script, tx and sighash plus a spec note. The agent ports the script interpreter (all opcodes, P2SH, segwit v0, taproot/tapscript validation rules, sighash computation, flags) to a Rust crate with a CLI that reads a JSON-lines verify request. The secp256k1 primitives are provided as a small provided crate.

full_card.band: 8h tier. Frontier agent can recall much of interpreter.cpp, so the risk is K8-style recall; exact flag and error-code fidelity on random hidden cases is the difficulty. Weaker models stall on segwit and taproot.
full_card.build_cost: 3-4 days: the oracle build is fiddly (probe red, fetch_ok false) and the 2.5k-line reference plus hidden-vector generation takes real time.
full_card.deliverable: Rust crate implementing script execution (all opcodes, P2SH, witness v0, taproot/tapscript, flags, error codes), sighash (legacy, BIP143, BIP341) and the CLI.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Ban linking or wrapping any Bitcoin C++ code (libbitcoinconsensus, bitcoinkernel) and ban network or vendored crates; the grader checks Cargo deps offline and rejects FFI. Hidden vectors are generated offline and never shipped, so memorising public JSON fails.
full_card.grading_surface: Repo vectors (thousands, count not verified) plus hidden vectors from the C++ oracle over random scripts and flag combinations; accept/reject plus error code.
full_card.local_fit: CPU-only Rust crate, fits 8 cores and 16 GB. The C++ oracle build is pipeline-side and needs boost and cmake, which the red probe did not complete.
full_card.lookup: partial: FFI wrappers (rust-bitcoin bitcoinconsensus, bitcoinkernel) and a non-consensus scriptexec exist; no public pure-Rust consensus port found.
full_card.provenance: bitcoin/bitcoin, MIT. Tag v31.1 exists; the tag's commit per the release page is 9be056a, not 4303f3b7 (4303f3b7 is likely main HEAD). Pin the commit before use.
full_card.reference: Seed claims a ~2.5k-line Rust port passing all vectors. Not public; must be built and verified by the pipeline.
full_card.ships: Data-driven vectors for script, tx and sighash (src/test/data JSON), a spec note, a provided secp256k1 crate, and a Rust crate skeleton with a JSON-lines CLI.
full_card.similarity: Nearest seeds S-im-014 (0.232), S-im-016 (0.184), S-im-012 (0.171) are other seeds, not public tasks. wasm_interpreter and sed_interpreter neighbours are interpreters, not the same subject. No CROWDED match.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agent results, so capped at 3.

Build.why: Oracle build is red in the probe, plus a 2.5k-line reference; roughly 3-4 days.

Fit.why: CPU Rust crate fits; oracle build is pipeline-side.

Hor.why: Real 8h scope: opcodes, flags, sighash, taproot each take hours.

Lic.why: MIT allows shipping the system, data and reference.

Multi.why: Opcodes, P2SH, segwit v0, taproot, sighash and flags give many buckets.

Nov.why: No public-task neighbour above 0.15 and no CROWDED match; S-im-014 is a seed, not a task.

Real.why: MIT Core repo, tag v31.1 and vector files confirmed; commit mismatch noted.

Ref.why: Claimed reference is private and unverified; no public complete port.

Seal.why: Oracle and hidden vectors are not in the image; the upstream C++ is not shipped, though it is recallable in outline.

Surf.why: Thousands of repo vectors plus an unlimited random generator from the C++ oracle.

spike_plan.kill_if: The C++ oracle cannot be built in the container within 60 min, vector output is nondeterministic, or the vector count is under about 1000.
spike_plan.pass_if: Oracle builds offline-reproducibly within 60 min, two runs give identical outputs, the vector count is in the thousands, and the stub passes at least 30% of a legacy sample.
steps: Clone bitcoin/bitcoin, check out tag v31.1 and separately commit 4303f3b7; record which commit matches the seed's vectors.

Configure cmake with tests on and bitcoin binaries off (e.g. -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DBUILD_BITCOIN_BIN=OFF -DBUILD_UTIL=OFF -DENABLE_WALLET=OFF) and build test_bitcoin; log missing deps against the apt hint.
Run test_bitcoin --run_test=script_tests, tx_tests and sighash_tests twice; count cases and check identical output.
Find or write a minimal harness that calls VerifyScript with a flag set and dumps accept/reject plus error code for a few hundred random scripts.
Write a 300-line Rust stub covering about 30 opcodes and legacy scripts, then measure the pass fraction on the script_tests sample.

v1.summary: The upstream repo, MIT licence and vector files are real, but the seed's commit 4303f3b7 does not match the v31.1 tag (which points to 9be056a), and the vector counts and the 2.5k-line reference are unverified. The idea is viable at Band 3 with build cost 3-4 days; the oracle build is red and must be fixed in the spike, and the recall risk is handled by sealing and by the exact-error-code grading.

v2.note: Real MIT source with a C++ oracle and an unlimited generator. The Rust reference does not exist and we must write and verify about 2.5k lines. Main K8 risk: interpreter.cpp and the btcd txscript port are famous, and shipping the full script_tests/tx_valid/sighash JSON gives a near-complete local oracle, so the frontier may average near the ceiling. Random scripts mostly fail early on trivial errors, so the generator must be structure-aware (valid P2SH, segwit and tapscript spends). Pin the v31.1 tag commit 9be056a. The oracle build was red. Build cost is 3-4 days.
